1.title: Security Features and Defense Techniques
1.text: Welcome to Module nineteen: Security Features and Defense Techniques. It covers the exam area four point zero Network Security. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. four point three Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques and solutions: device hardening (disable unused ports and services, change default passwords). Network access control (port security, eight oh two dot one X, M A C filtering). Key management. Security rules (A C L, U R L filtering, content filtering). Zones (trusted versus untrusted, screened subnet). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four point zero Network Security (fourteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Device hardening
1.text: Device hardening. Disable unused ports and services. Fewer ways in: shut down unused switch ports, turn off Telnet, H T T P, unused protocols. Change default passwords. Default credentials are public; use strong, unique passwords. Patch and update firmware. Fix known vulnerabilities. Use secure management. S S H, H T T P S, S N M P version three instead of Telnet, H T T P, S N M P version two C. Exam tip: The first hardening steps on a new device: change default credentials, disable unneeded services, and shut down unused ports.

1.title: Network access control (NAC)
1.text: Network access control (N A C). N A C checks a device and user before allowing it on the network. Port security. Limits which and how many M A C addresses a switch port accepts; violation modes: protect, restrict, shutdown. eight oh two dot one X. Port-based authentication: the supplicant (device) authenticates through the authenticator (switch or A P) to a R A D I U S server using E A P over L A N (E A Po L). M A C filtering. Allows or denies by M A C address; easy but weak (M A Cs can be spoofed).

1.title: Network access control (NAC), continued
1.text: Network access control (N A C). The figure shows this: eight oh two dot one X: supplicant, authenticator and R A D I U S server.

1.title: Security rules and key management
1.text: Security rules and key management. A C L (access control list). Ordered permit and deny rules on a router, switch or firewall by source, destination, protocol and port; processed top down; first match wins; ends with an implicit deny. U R L filtering. Blocks or allows websites by address or category. Content filtering. Blocks traffic by what it contains (malware, file types, keywords, categories). Key management. Generating, storing, rotating and revoking cryptographic keys securely. Exam tip: A C Ls end with an implicit "deny all", so a missing permit blocks traffic. Put specific rules before general rules.

1.title: Zones
1.text: Zones. Trusted. The internal network. Untrusted. The internet or any outside network. Screened subnet (formerly D M Z). A buffer network between trusted and untrusted that holds public-facing servers (web, mail); a compromise there does not give direct access to the internal network. Exam tip: A C Ls are read top down and end with an implicit deny. Exam tip: A screened subnet holds public servers between the internet and the internal network.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A technician installs a new switch. Which action is part of device hardening? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Changing the default password and disabling unused ports. Hardening removes defaults and unneeded exposure.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A switch port must allow only one specific workstation. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Port security with a sticky M A C address. Port security limits the M A C addresses on a port.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Devices must authenticate to a R A D I U S server before the switch port is enabled. Which standard is used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: eight oh two dot one X. eight oh two dot one X provides port-based authentication.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Public web servers must be reachable from the internet but isolated from the internal L A N. Where should they be placed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: In a screened subnet. A screened subnet limits exposure of the internal network.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A firewall A C L has a permit rule for H T T P but traffic on port eight thousand eighty is blocked. Why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The implicit deny at the end of the A C L drops it. Traffic that matches no rule hits the implicit deny.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which control blocks employees from visiting gambling sites by category? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: U R L filtering. U R L filtering blocks sites by address or category.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does eight oh two dot one X provide? Answer: Port-based network access authentication. Question two. What is the implicit rule at the end of an A C L? Answer: Deny all. Question three. Why is M A C filtering weak? Answer: M A C addresses can be spoofed.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is a screened subnet? Answer: A buffer network between trusted and untrusted networks that holds public-facing servers. Question five. What does port security limit? Answer: The M A C addresses allowed on a switch port. Question six. Name two hardening steps. Answer: Change default passwords and disable unused ports and services.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Hardening: change defaults, disable unused ports and services, patch, secure management. N A C: port security (M A C limits), eight oh two dot one X (R A D I U S, E A Po L), M A C filtering (weak). Rules: A C L (top down, implicit deny), U R L filtering, content filtering, key management. Zones: trusted, untrusted, screened subnet.
